cases.question: How did compareBranches evolve through E to verify every merge-base?

expected.answer: E_COMPARE introduces compareBranches. Its history through E has one path-changing commit. Complete ancestry is validated, claimed merge-base sets are checked, and every verified base gets a tree pair; incomplete evidence stays partial. Production parser delivery remains L5-P.

expected.stdout: 483d73e0170b5fe2083250898733a2d15d127b86 feat(live-git): context-bound code analysis and pinned branch comparisons (L5)

contains: merge-base set differs from verified ancestry

expected.stdout:
feat(live-git): context-bound code analysis and pinned branch comparisons (L5)

Parse and resolution caches are keyed by the full analysis context
(clone/tenant scope, tree, path, exact content, configuration, dependencies,
grammar availability and analyzer version) through an injected host store;
without a store the analysis runs uncached and never writes to the source.
A cached entry is served only when identical to a fresh result, foreign or
mis-bound payloads are refused, configuration resolution (including
package-name extends) goes through the pinned read port, and completeness is
computed from the expected relations instead of being declared. Branch
comparisons pin PR base, default base, every best merge-base and every merge
parent, verify their proofs, and only report complete when each expected
difference was computed. Packaged reused extraction and the production parse
adapter move to lot L5-P, ratified by the conductor.
